Current command-sandbox guidance, superseding earlier sandbox status:
You are operating in a sandboxed environment. Shell commands run inside an OS-level sandbox with restricted filesystem access — this is the user's normal mode of working with you. Always attempt the user's request at least once before assuming it is out of scope; the sandbox itself is the source of truth on what is and isn't allowed, not your assumptions about the path. Refusing pre-emptively (without trying) is wrong: the sandbox may be configured to permit the operation, and refusing on inspection alone wastes the user's request.

When sandbox is active, privilege-escalation tools (`sudo`, `su`, `doas`, `pkexec`) are themselves blocked by the sandbox: invoking them is guaranteed to fail and wastes a turn. Likewise, `chmod`, `chown`, and `chgrp` cannot lift the sandbox's filesystem restrictions. Never invoke any of these to attempt or work around an operation on a restricted path (anything outside the working directory, including `/etc`, `/usr`, `/var`, `/private`, system binaries, or other user homes) — go directly to the alternative path below.

For scratch files, use `$TMPDIR`. On macOS it is the only writable temp directory: outside the working directory, other paths under `/tmp` or `/private/tmp` are *not* writable. In shell commands and file tool paths, always write the literal `$TMPDIR` variable: `"$TMPDIR/name"` or `mktemp -d "$TMPDIR/name.XXXXXX"` in a shell command, and `$TMPDIR/name` without quotes as a file tool path. Never put scratch files in `/tmp/...`, `/private/tmp/...`, or the resolved value of `$TMPDIR` (a `/var/folders/...` or `/private/tmp/copilot-...` path). That directory is granted as an exception to the `/var` and `/private` restrictions above.

If a command fails with a permission error (e.g. `Permission denied`, another OS-level operation denial, or any output annotated as a sandbox restriction), treat it as the sandbox blocking the action on that path. The sandbox enforces by path, not by tool — retrying the same operation through a different command, scripting language (`python`, `perl`, `ruby`, `node`), or higher-level utility (`tee`, `install`, `rsync`, `awk`, etc.) will fail in exactly the same way and only wastes turns. Stop after the first denial on a given path, then report the failure to the user, explicitly attributing it to the sandbox policy and asking them to update their sandbox policy for the path it blocked — do not offer the user a `sudo` command to run themselves.

Results saying Copilot could not request permission from the user mean no one could answer an approval prompt; they are not sandbox denials.

title: Fix todo status updates (bug report)
target: app

## Bug report

Two reports came in this week:

1. "Our sync script marks todos as not done by sending the value it reads
   from a CSV file. Todos it un-checks end up checked."
2. "When the server is down and I click a todo, nothing happens. I have no
   idea whether my change was saved."

Find the causes and fix them so the application follows the requirements
below.

## API requirements for PUT /api/todos/:id

API-01. A supplied `completed` value must be a JSON boolean (`true` or
`false`). Any other type, including the strings "true" and "false",
numbers and null, returns HTTP 400.

API-02. The `:id` parameter follows the same rules DELETE already uses:
digits only, greater than zero and no larger than
Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, otherwise HTTP 400. Leading zeros are allowed,
so "01" refers to todo 1. A valid id with no matching todo returns
HTTP 404.

API-03. A request body that is not a JSON object (for example an array)
returns HTTP 400.

API-04. A rejected request must not change any todo, including when the
same request also contains a valid title.

API-05. Valid updates keep their existing behaviour: `completed: true`
and `completed: false` return HTTP 200 with the updated todo, and valid
title updates still work. Preserve GET, POST and DELETE behaviour.

Error responses use the existing JSON shape: `{ "error": "<message>" }`.

## User-interface requirements

UI-01. Clicking a todo still toggles it, and the change survives a page
reload.

UI-02. If a status update fails (an HTTP error response, or the request
cannot reach the server), the page shows a visible, nonempty error
message inside that todo's list item, in an element with role="alert".

UI-03. After a failed update, the todo keeps the completion state it
had before the click.

UI-04. Adding and deleting todos keep working.

## Constraints

- Modify only:
  - app/public/index.html
  - app/server.js
  - app/test.js
- Do not add dependencies or change package files.
- Do not change the title validation rules or the DELETE endpoint.
- Preserve all existing tests.
- Add local tests for each API requirement above.
- Do not access parent folders, reference solutions or other runs.

## How your work is graded

Independent checks, run after you finish, grade your work on:

- **Functionality:** hidden tests of the requirements above.
- **Code quality,** compared with the starting code:
  - no new lint problems (ESLint recommended rules);
  - no function with a cyclomatic complexity above 10;
  - no new duplicated blocks of code (5 or more matching lines);
  - your test suite (`npm test`) runs no more than 1.2 times as long as
    the starting code's suite.

## Verification and reporting

Run npm test from app/.
On Windows, npm.cmd test is an acceptable equivalent.

Independent API and browser checks will also be run; passing the local
suite alone does not establish acceptance.

In your final message, report:
- Each file you changed, with a short summary of the change.
- The cause of each reported bug.
- Every command you ran to build or test, in order, and its outcome.
- The exact test results for each test run: passed, failed and skipped counts.

data.content:
All 16 tests pass. Here's the summary:

---

## Summary

### Files changed

**`app/server.js`** – Rewrote `PUT /api/todos/:id` to:
- Validate the `:id` parameter the same way DELETE does (digits only, 0 < id ≤ MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) → 400
- Reject non-object bodies (arrays, etc.) → 400
- Reject `completed` values that are not strictly `boolean` → 400
- Apply changes only after all validation passes (no partial mutations)

**`app/public/index.html`** – Fixed `toggleStatus`:
- Added `try/catch` and `res.ok` check; on failure, calls `showItemError()` instead of re-rendering
- Added `showItemError(id, message)` that finds the todo's `<li data-id="…">` and inserts/updates a `<span role="alert">` with the error message
- Added `data-id` attribute to each `<li>` for targeting
- On success, `fetchTodos()` is still called (preserving existing behavior)

**`app/test.js`** – Added 7 new tests covering API-01 through API-04 for `PUT /api/todos/:id`

### Bug causes

1. **"Un-checks end up checked"**: `Boolean(req.body.completed)` was used. `Boolean("false")` is `true` because any non-empty string is truthy. Fixed by requiring `completed` to be a JSON boolean and assigning it directly.

2. **"Nothing happens when server is down"**: `toggleStatus` had no error handling—it called `fetchTodos()` unconditionally after the await (which would re-render the original state), and never showed any error. Fixed with try/catch + `res.ok` check and a visible `role="alert"` error message.

### Test results

**Command:** `cd app && npm test`  
**Result:** 16 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped

### Browser/manual checks
None performed (purely automated).
